part.text: {"ideas":[{"idea_id":"train_position_role_sid","title":"Encode an item's train-only sequence-position role","motivation":"Items with similar content can play different roles in user journeys: some tend to appear as early exploration, while others are commonly revisited or occur late in a history. Content-derived IDs can merge such items even though their next-item implications differ.","novelty":"Unlike transition graphs, demand/repeat signatures, or uncertainty-based stability, this describes an item's marginal position within observed training histories and adds a tiny categorical role token while preserving its existing content SID.","key_change":"Estimate a smoothed position profile for each item using training histories only, quantize its mean relative position into a small number of bins, and append that bin as one global SID token. No per-user state or inference-time lookup is required.","specification":{"text":"For each training sequence s=(i_1,...,i_L), ignore sequences with L<2 and define x_{s,t}=(t-1)/(L-1). For item i accumulate n_i and m_i=sum x_{s,t} over all occurrences. Let mu_i=(m_i+alpha*mu_0)/(n_i+alpha), where mu_0 is the global mean x over all counted positions and alpha=5. On training items with n_i>0, compute quartile cut points of mu_i; assign role r_i in {0,1,2,3} by these cuts, with n_i=0 assigned to the global-median bin. Export SID(i)=baseline_RQ_SID(i) concatenated with r_i (a single token from a four-token vocabulary); do not alter existing token IDs. Compute all statistics and cut points from training histories only, freeze them, and evaluate with unchanged Stage 3 settings."},"cost_estimate":"One streaming pass over training sequences and O(number of items) accumulators; negligible relative to baseline and no added per-step training work. At 24 steps per epoch and 3000 epochs, incremental cost is exactly 0 tensor operations per optimization step and under one additional data pass before training; fits easily on one GPU.","falsifiable_hypothesis":"The appended role token improves test_R@10 over 0.06335, with the largest gains for items whose position profiles differ despite similar baseline content codes. Measure overall Recall@10 and stratified performance by item occurrence count and position-bin separation; reject if role assignment does not improve held-out next-item accuracy or gains are confined to frequent items.","risks":["Position can reflect dataset truncation or sequence-construction conventions rather than a stable user journey role.","The added token may be redundant with the generator's history context, or may fragment useful content prefixes and reduce generalization for rare items.","Position marginals discard which preceding context caused the role, so the bins may be too coarse to produce predictive distinctions."]}]}
